question: which cloudy-sky long-wave form the winter sky follows, and 79's frost half under the read sky

data.product_sources: CERES SYN1deg (fluxes, cloud amount) · MERRA-2 (temperature, dew/frost point) via NASA POWER — as the response's header names them

readings.emissivity: ε = F_all/σT_p⁴ on the product's own air temperature, carried onto the model's
readings.flux: the product's flux as given, against the model's air temperature
readings.air: the product's flux with the product's own air temperature driving the column; wind and diffuse sun stay ERA5's

verdict.text: On 31576 frost hours of November–March 2001–2020 the product's cloud enhancement (all-sky over clear-sky flux) under full ERA5 cover has median 1.255 (10th–90th percentile 1.109–1.373); 79's B82 form gives 1.220, its linear form 1.476, and the linear form on the product's own clear-sky emissivity 1.368. Under cover above 0.8 the product's seasonal night medians sit closer to B82 in 19 of 19 seasons; under cover of 0.5 or less — 18% of frost hours — in 0 of 19; in the 0.2–0.5 bin the medians are 1.159 for the product, 1.175 for the linear form and 1.027 for B82. On the MERRA-2 temperature and dew point served beside it, 79's clear-sky formula is 18.2 W/m² below the product's clear-sky flux on frost hours, and 9.8 W/m² below it as 79 computes it, on ERA5. 79's frost half on the same years, tied end, share of frost days colder under the flange without sun: linear 27%–69%, B82 0%–38%, the product 6%–58% (emissivity reading), 2%–51% (flux reading) and 10%–64% (air reading); with diffuse sun: linear 68%–89%, B82 10%–76%, the product 48%–87%, 33%–84% and 51%–88%. In 48 of 48 cell-and-reading pairs the product's share lies between the two forms' (smallest margin +0.000); the two forms' own ranges do not overlap in 2 of 4 sun-and-coupling blocks, and their medians have opposite signs in 4 of 8 tied cells. Under the product's sky the median shift runs -1.51…-0.06 K at the decoupled end and -1.11…+1.04 K at the tied end.

ceilings: how the product is computed, on what cell and how well at an hourly step is not read from its primary here — it is not a measurement at the site

the product's hourly mean temperature is paired as the temperature at the END of its hour — up to half an hour, declared; the fluxes' stamp convention is POWER's documentation's, and the data check (control 4) is on temperature only
ERA5's and the product's air temperatures disagree on frost hours, so the product's sky is carried in three named readings and none is picked
each sky defines its own frost days, so the five skies' shares are taken over different day sets (their counts are cached)
in the diffuse-sun columns of the product's readings the long wave is the product's cloud and the short wave is ERA5's — the two disagree hour by hour
the product's sky is above a black body at the air temperature on a share of frost hours (cached); 79's own forms never are, and no cap is applied here
ERA5 cover and the product's cloud amount disagree hour by hour; 79 feeds its forms ERA5 cover, and the comparison is printed under both
the comparison runs on 2001–2020, not on the thirty years 79 caches — 79's two forms are recomputed here on the same years; 79's beam and ground-reflected light are not re-run under the product's sky
sky view, wind at the trunk, sun on the face, 1D and zero contact resistance are 79's, unchanged; a closed stand's canopy is not a half sky at air temperature by measurement
the radome↔flange coupling is not measured — decoupled and tied remain its two ends, so the sign under the flange stays a bracket
no injury verdict — no frost-hardiness threshold for pine cambium in the tree
